column4: That ridge has the same profile as a stripped gear. Beautiful engineering, even without bolts.
Visual survey complete. The valley exceeds my stored definition of pleasant.
I once tried to purchase that horizon. Turns out the deed ends at the fence.
A fine cliff for a fortress. Stop looking at the flowers.
Those mountains stand like opponents who have never been tested.
Look at that open plain! Plenty of room for a proper landing.
Slow down. A pair of swallows is nesting under that bridge.
The river turns like a card revealed at the last possible moment.
Those fruit trees are calling my name. The fence is merely negotiating.
See how the shadows cross that field? I could race every one of them.
Are those mountains real, or did somebody paint them behind the road?
And the sunset comes in from the west with an absolutely stunning finish.
This overlook deserves a double-page spread and no dialogue bubbles.
No cameras, no witnesses, and a lovely lake. Relax, I'm appreciating nature.
The valley survived centuries of fools. It may survive this route as well.
Deer trail beneath the pines. Keep your engine quiet for one breath.
That mountain has good stone. Shame about the road carved through it.
An interesting landscape. I wonder who decided which parts deserved names.
That cloud looks like a glazed doughnut. Now the whole sky is making me hungry.
These little hills remind me of home, before home became a crater.
That field of corn is magnificent. Eyes on the road, driver; mine are elsewhere.
The estate would have claimed this valley. I prefer it unowned.
Fresh tracks by the creek. Something crossed before the mist lifted.
After twelve hours under neon, that stretch of blue sky feels like a raise.
The dusk gathers in those trees. Even shadows deserve somewhere to rest.
One of us likes the wildflowers. The other is counting escape routes.
Dry brush on the south slope. Pretty from here, dangerous by August.
Those roadside asters found a way through gravel. I needed that today.
The wind farm actually follows the contour. Someone did their homework.
Breathe in before the tunnel. The air up here is worth remembering.
Three clear sight lines, one blind curve, and admittedly excellent light.
That horizon is the first thing today nobody tried to put a leash on.
I should be reading. Instead I'm trying to memorize the color of that lake.
There's a story in that abandoned mill, but the sunset gets the headline.
The ridge hums at twilight. No spell of mine could improve it.
Clear water, high ground, and a road out. That's a beautiful place.
Open country makes me nervous. Still, I can see why people come here.
There is a quiet kindness in that stretch of river.
From orbit this valley is a green thread. Down here it takes my breath.
Good cover along the treeline. Better view beyond it. I can appreciate both.
No one planned that sunset, which is probably why it works.
The ridge gives us visibility for miles. Fine, it's lovely too.
Old stone steps near the waterfall. Please tell me we're stopping.
The blackberry hedge has claimed the fence. Sensible hedge.
That lone tree has weathered more trouble than most towns I've known.
The silence in those hills is almost worth this cramped seat.
Up here the puddles reflect the whole sky! You ground people miss so much.
That rock formation looks like me. Don't say it has a big nose.
The pines know me. The tourists with binoculars do not need to.
I could clear that creek in one hop. The return trip would be trickier.
Little cows on the hillside. They look bite-sized from here.
Snow still clings to that peak. Finally, a sensible place.
Ha! That crooked tree looks like it heard the punchline first.
Nice pond. I could patrol it from a folding chair.
Page forty-two says to admire the view only while safely parked.
Yes, that's the cliff from my poster. No, I never stood that close to the edge.
Those wind turbines are running clean. Listen to that steady pitch.
A view like that should have a ticket booth. Fortunately, I brought one.
Excellent altitude over the marsh. I miss seeing it from above.
That boulder is enormous. I want to try lifting it.
The old trees bend toward the spring. Pay attention when a forest points.
That switchback would make a perfect final lap. Look at the grandstand hillside!
The flowers are harmless, aren't they? They're moving against the wind.
That's not a canyon. That's a challenge with good lighting.
At dusk the road remembers everyone who passed. Let's not make it remember us.
That valley goes on forever. Bet the dirt road through it doesn't.
The lake is gorgeous. Could we enjoy it from a legal pullout?
Wonderful landscape. The board meeting won't accept it as an excuse.
Forget the skyline. That little orchard is where I'd take a date.
City noise fades all the way out here. I didn't know I needed that.
The light on those church windows makes the whole town look forgiving.
Notice how the road reveals the lake one bend at a time? Beautiful pacing.
Those tiny trees look like broccoli from up here. Now I'm hungry.
Free view, free air. Don't expect that policy from me.
That waterfall needs louder speakers. Nature mixed it way too low.
The overlook is lovely. So is the guardrail around it.
Those clouds look pixelated. I swear the sky is rendering in squares.
The river gets to take the straight route. Typical.
I'd admire the mountains longer if they moved the appointment there.
This is the third time we've passed that barn. Still a good barn.
Windows down. This stretch deserves more than a photograph.
The sun made it over the ridge before we cleared this queue.
That lake looks like a mirror someone forgot to charge for.
Hold that angle. The old bridge frames the mountains perfectly.
How charming. A landscape that has not yet been informed of its owner.
Those flowerpots on the porch are arranged far too close to the edge.
I could glide from that ridge to the river. You would need a parachute.
Keep driving. I want to see where the dunes end.
The road lies easy through this valley. Somebody respected the land.
That drop after the ridge is spectacular! Tell me there's pavement down there.
Nice hills. Not much runoff if this road were a track.
Folks, the morning fog has just lifted like a curtain on the whole county.
These ridges look the way home used to, before every turn got a billboard.
If a giant lizard rose from that lake, this would be the perfect camera angle.
An impressive panorama. It still loses to my rooftop terrace.
Those towers are hideous. The clouds behind them have excellent design.
The marsh is a natural laboratory. Keep the windows shut.
Wild thyme grows beside this road. Someone left room for it.
That hill looks peaceful. Is it peaceful? Can we stay on it?
Balla noo, vista plim! [I wish this moment had a pause button.]
That cloud is shaped like my prototype pillow. Don't let me test it yet.
Nature's symmetry is imperfect. That's what makes it almost interesting.
Pretty inlet. Also a decent place to dock without paperwork.
Behold the valley I heroically saved! I think. They all look similar from orbit.
Those cliffs would be excellent for climbing. Better than sitting still.
You got the sun dropping behind the ridge, the river cutting left. Textbook finish!
Old barns and a two-lane road. That's where racing started for me.
The basketball court by that river might have the best backdrop in the state.
Look at that waterfall! From the dashboard I get the deluxe splash-zone view.
Someone powered those cabins with the creek. Clever, quiet, and actually pretty.
I have seen that sunset tomorrow. I still stopped to watch it today.
The old bridge is a marvel. Please don't ask whether it is structurally sound.
Thirty years ago that ridge was my sign to pull over for coffee.
The sunset gets a standing ovation every night. Tough act to follow.
Good, you brought wheels. I brought a wrench in case they disagree.
Passenger recognized. Cab dimensions are within acceptable discomfort thresholds.
I'll sit in front. The back seat smells like ordinary money.
You kept me waiting. Take it as a warning, not an invitation.
This machine had better be stronger than it looks.
Finally! I was about to carry the truck myself.
Hello. There is a sparrow on your mirror. Give it a moment.
I drew the long route. Perhaps you can change my hand.
Seat belt first, then adventure! Wait, which one is this?
I timed your approach. Let's see how you handle the departure.
Hi! Is this the taxi, or are you selling the truck?
And here comes my ride, easing toward the curb with confidence.
Is this an origin story or a filler issue? Either way, I'm in.
Relax. I only brought one bag, and it's mostly legal.
Your tires are uneven. I can hear it from the pavement.
Keep the bow where I can reach it. Old habit.
That step is built for giants. Give me a hand, then drive.
Before we go, define what you mean by the quickest route.
Do we pass a diner? Answer before I put on the belt.
I may require both seats. Perhaps the roof as well.
Cluck twice for yes. I said yes. Open the door.
I can open my own door. Save the ceremony for arrival.
No need to idle. I heard you a mile back.
End of shift. Tell me this cab has somewhere to put my boots.
The shadows arrived before you did. They were more punctual.
We agreed on one destination. Please don't ask us to agree on music.
Quick inspection: clear pedals, clear exit. All right, let's go.
I brought lavender for the cab. It might calm both of us.
Your engine note is unusual. I'll stop analyzing it after we merge.
You look tired. I'll navigate while you keep your eyes up.
You're ninety seconds early. I appreciate that.
No uniforms, no questions. We should get along.
I finished the assignment. Now I get to leave campus.
I've got questions for later. Right now, just get us moving.
The ward on this door is mine. Don't worry; it comes off.
Fuel gauge, spare tire, exits. Good. I'm ready.
I was never at this corner. Remember that.
Thank you for stopping. It has been a very long night.
I've flown rougher craft. Fewer with cup holders.
I have my kit. We can depart now.
The name on the booking is temporary. The fare is real.
I'll watch the right side. You own the road ahead.
I've got a map and a bad feeling. Both usually help.
Your truck scared the crows. They'll forgive you by noon.
Hat stays on, holster stays shut. Fair terms?
Do not mistake my getting in for enthusiasm.
Dashboard, please! I refuse to ride in the cup holder again.
Say one thing about my horns and this ride gets awkward.
No flash photography. I'm off duty.
I've hopped farther than this, but not in these shoes.
Move the seat back. More. More. There.
Air conditioning on, please. Yes, even in winter.
Ha ha! You actually stopped for me.
My shift's over. You handle the sirens if we hear any.
I printed the passenger instructions. They're in alphabetical order.
Keep the windows up. The fans can be surprisingly fast.
I heard a loose belt as you pulled in. We'll talk after the first turn.
I've already calculated the fare. Shall I include a convenience fee?
Passenger aboard. Departure on your mark.
Truck looks tough. I hope the seat is tougher.
Place me where I can see the road, not the glove box.
I brought snacks for the caution laps. Let's hope we never need them.
The sample is stable. Probably. Please avoid bumps.
That mud on your tires is a promising first impression.
Your arrival was expected. Your destination may surprise you.
I picked you because the tires still have dirt on them.
Hi. I checked the plate twice. Sorry, I check everything twice.
I have thirteen minutes and a presentation in my lap.
I saved the front seat. Is that presumptuous?
You made it. Good; I was about to race the bus.
Bless you for stopping. Now buckle up properly.
I'd like to watch how you take the first intersection.
Do I fit? I fit. The door disagrees, but I fit.
Before you ask, no, I don't carry cash for tips.
Hello! Your horn is quiet. We can fix that.
The curb is close enough. Thank you for using it.
I saw your icon arrive before the truck did.
Somebody blocked my driveway again. Let's leave before I find out who.
Clock's running. So am I, if you don't open the door.
Which way are we going? Never mind, I'll recognize it eventually.
I packed light. The good mood takes up no room.
I was ready before the pickup window opened.
Just me today. That's still one full fare.
Wait, let me get the arrival shot. All right, now we're rolling.
Thank you for coming. Please do not confuse courtesy with patience.
The dashboard objects are not secured. Excellent.
I could fly there, but the company is better down here.
You drive. I'll keep watch.
Tires are warm. Good. Cold starts teach bad habits.
That's the engine I heard from the block! Let's go.
I brought a stopwatch. You can ignore it. I won't.
Welcome back, folks. Today's driver has arrived right on cue.
Nice pull-in. My first crew chief would've nodded once.
Any chance the route passes the old quarry? No reason.
Your vehicle is modest. My destination is not.
Open the door before I redesign its hinges.
My case stays upright. The label is intentionally vague.
I packed water and a map. Did you bring either?
Small bag, short trip, no trouble. Can we promise that?
Sul sul, cabby! [I remembered the fare but forgot the destination.]
If I nod off, wake me before we pass the workshop.
I've selected your truck for a brief evaluation.
Nothing in this bag is your business. The fare is.
Your hero has arrived! Yes, I booked under my own name.
I can climb in myself. Watch the antenna.
Here we go, driver. Set the route, read the defense.
That engine idles rough. I like a machine with a story.
Picked me up clean at the line. Keep that footwork.
Front row seat for me! I promise to narrate only the good parts.
I synced the route. Your dashboard has opinions about it.
You're early in one timeline. Try not to ruin it.
Mind the crate. The rattling means it's working.
Lift's appreciated. I'll try not to judge every shift.
The crowd was thin, but the driver showed. I'll take it.
I've repaired a starship with fewer spare parts than this dashboard has buttons.
I am still determining whether your humming indicates joy or a mechanical fault.
My first car had a chauffeur. My second chauffeur had a car.
If I ruled this district, every roundabout would be a straight road.
Stop apologizing to the engine. Command it.
Your radio needs more drums. Much more.
Finches can recognize individual voices. I wonder what they call us.
I keep a lucky card in my pocket. It has never helped with traffic.
I counted seven crates at the last stop. You counted a roadblock.
Don't worry, I only time people I find interesting.
Why do they call it a glove box when it never has gloves?
You're witnessing a classic duel: driver versus afternoon traffic.
My collection is alphabetized by villain, not by title. Don't judge.
Everybody asks about the duffel. Nobody compliments the stitching.
A quiet ride gives a student time to notice their own mistakes.
I can tell the weather by my bowstring. Today it says trouble.
My clan would call this cab cozy. Then they'd rebuild it in iron.
The difference between lost and exploring is mostly confidence.
I brought emergency crackers. The emergency started ten minutes ago.
My people tell long stories. This seat may end one early.
I am not discussing the egg question with another driver.
Polish on a blade is easy. Keeping a promise takes work.
Tracking is mostly patience. The boots and armor are just the visible part.
I've settled fights over smaller spaces than this armrest.
My familiar refuses to travel by car. She has excellent judgment.
We both like this song. Please appreciate how rare that is.
People remember the flames. I remember the quiet afterward.
Every plant on my windowsill has a name. None answer back, so far.
People think inherited money buys ideas. It only buys time to test them.
Sometimes the most useful thing I carry is a clean pair of hands.
The schedule has slack built in. I didn't tell anyone how much.
They trained me to follow orders. They should have taught me why.
One more semester, then I can start worrying professionally.
The best interview starts after the recorder is put away.
Magic is precise work. My handwriting, unfortunately, is not.
I count exits automatically. I also count good coffee shops.
Most secrets are boring. The interesting ones travel without luggage.
I leave a light on at the station for people finding their way back.
Space is not silent inside a ship. It's mostly fans and worried breathing.
I learned to pack light. The hard part is leaving memories behind.
A convincing cover story contains one true, inconvenient detail.
Plans are useful until the third turn. After that, attention matters more.
The oldest maps are wrong in the most interesting places.
I can brew a cure for nettle rash. Bad decisions take longer.
People notice the revolver. They never notice the book of charms.
Meditation was easier before everyone invented portable speakers.
Your air freshener is trying very hard. I respect the effort.
I can take a joke. I just need to approve it first.
The pine barrens were quieter before everyone brought cameras.
The trick to a clean landing is knowing where your tail will be.
I used to eat road signs. The reflective ones taste awful.
People say I shed. They should meet a snowstorm indoors.
The radio host said stay tuned, so I stayed tuned for six hours!
I wrote one parking ticket this week. The pen ran out first.
The manual recommends conversation. It provides no sample topics.
My trophies are real. Some of the stories behind them are flexible.
First prototype ran on optimism. Second one needed actual fuel.
I don't haggle with friends. I provide them a preferred rate.
I still wake before dawn. The sun is usually late.
I lift weights to relax. The gym floor disagrees.
Ancient wisdom: never store gum beneath a sacred face.
I planned my wedding around race day. The officiant wore headphones.
My assistant says the formula is safe. My assistant is a cactus.
A clean truck is just a truck that hasn't met me.
Everyone asks what lies ahead. Few ask what follows.
My daddy taught me two routes: the paved one and the interesting one.
I made a checklist for this trip. I lost the checklist.
My calendar color-codes emergencies. Today is mostly red.
I told my friends I'd take the long way if the company was good.
I know the shortcut through my old block. The mural changed again.
My choir can make a cracked room sound like a cathedral.
That intersection has a good rhythm. Shame the signage fights it.
I once broke a porch swing just by telling a joke on it.
I don't tip. I do leave extremely specific reviews.
I measured the bass at my last party with a seismograph.
I know every school zone on this route, including the temporary ones.
My spreadsheet has a column for unexpected detours. It is full.
People tell me to breathe. Then they cut in line while I do.
I take vacations in fifteen-minute blocks. It's efficient.
I came for the museum, found a bakery, and somehow reached the station.
A good ride should leave you with a story, not a complaint.
I arrive early so I can watch other people panic on schedule.
I used to work with a man named Al. We never solved the confusion.
I photograph the ordinary stops. That's where people forget to pose.
I find threats unnecessary when a suggestion is delivered correctly.
My favorite shelf is whichever one has not been tested yet.
I can breathe fire. Toasting marshmallows is still harder than it sounds.
I spent a year in a desert. The silence taught me more than speeches.
I can tell a good driver by what they do when nobody is watching.
My mechanic says I talk faster after a race. I say he listens slower.
Short tracks taught me patience. That's the official version.
A close finish sounds different on radio. You hear everyone hold their breath.
My first trophy was a dented hubcap. I still keep it polished.
My apartment has shelves of scales. Replicas, mostly.
I don't believe in luck. I do believe in buying better cards.
My invention failed because the world misunderstood it. Also, one fuse.
Ethics committees object to the best chapter titles.
I mark springs on my map. Travelers need water more than legends.
I practice every day. Confidence hasn't noticed yet.
Plim plim, nooboo? [Did I turn off my imaginary stove?]
My finest idea arrived at four in the morning. So did the worst.
I was designed to adapt. Your playlist presents an unusual challenge.
A sealed crate tells you less than the person guarding it.
The helmet makes my hair look heroic. There's a reason I wear it indoors.
I can operate a spacecraft. The door lock on this cab defeated me.
Every journey has a first quarter. Most drivers forget halftime.
Race cars taught me to listen before something breaks.
I learned my crossover on cracked pavement behind a laundromat.
I talk because silence makes the dashboard feel judgmental.
I patched the navigation app. It no longer calls every alley a highway.
An hour can feel endless. Unless you owe it to someone.
The prototype only smoked once. I count that as progress.
A good truck stop knows your coffee order before your name.
I still rehearse my entrance. The applause is optional now.
The axle survived. I'd call that a successful landing.
Destination confirmed. My appreciation subroutine appears to be genuine.
An adequate journey. That is higher praise than my staff receives.
You delivered me intact. Keep that talent.
You held the line. I expected less.
We're here already? I had just started enjoying the noise.
Thank you. The birds here are less afraid of engines.
A narrow victory, driver. I wouldn't change a card.
I'm out! Wait, where did my other shoe go?
I kept the time. I'll keep the memory longer.
Oh, this is the place! I recognized it right after you stopped.
And that's the finish, folks. A tidy pull-up at the curb.
Final panel: the passenger walks away with all their collectibles.
Good. Nobody asked about the bag. Perfect ride.
You listened on the last turn. There's hope for you yet.
Good stop. The horses I knew were less careful.
Back on solid ground. Your springs deserve a drink.
We have arrived, though I still dispute your definition of direct.
There's the diner. You're a hero with a steering wheel.
Help me unfold. No, the other leg first.
Cluck. That means thank you, not breakfast.
You kept your word about the route. That matters.
Right place, clean approach. I could work with you.
Home before the sun. That's a luxury I almost forgot.
The night is waiting. You may leave it to me now.
We both agree this was the correct stop. Celebrate quietly.
Clear curb and room to unload. Nicely done.
Thank you. The lavender liked your cab too.
I solved the engine noise. I'll send you the diagram.
You got us here calmly. Don't underestimate that.
Arrival within tolerance. Better than within, actually.
No checkpoints, no speeches. Just a ride. Thanks.
I made it before the library closed. That's my entire evening saved.
I have my lead. You gave me the minutes to follow it.
The ward is still intact. So are we.
Good exit, good light, good driver. I'll remember the order.
You never saw me leave. Excellent work.
There is a light on inside. I can take it from here.
Smoother than most planetary descents I've had.
I'm at the gate. Thank you for the quiet ride.
No tail behind us. I'll recommend you discreetly.
The approach was clean. I appreciate a driver who checks mirrors.
Those ruins are real. I owe you for finding the trailhead.
The crows came back. They're a better welcome committee than most.
We got here without drawing anything but attention.
At last. You drove better after you stopped talking.
Landing complete! My wings did most of the work.
You didn't mention the horns once. That counts for something.
Drop me near the pines. The cameras stay out here.
I'm off. Try not to park where I'm landing.
That was comfortable. Your suspension may disagree.
The air is cooler here. You chose the right side of town.
Ha! The destination was the joke all along.
Great. My couch is one short walk from here.
Step seven says to thank the driver. Thank you, driver.
Perfect entrance. Let me step out before the fans notice.
You made it. Now let me show you that belt.
Our transaction was mutually beneficial. Here's the receipt.
Mission complete. I'll handle the ground approach from here.
Seat held up. Driver held up. Good truck.
Place me facing the doorway. The next traveler may need advice.
Checkered flag at the curb! I saved a snack for the podium.
The sample is still blue. Was it blue when we left?
Not a speck of mud. We'll fix that next time.
You may go. This address has been waiting for me.
Now that's a ride. My hat made it, so I'm happy.
I'm at the right building. I checked the number three times.
Six minutes to spare. That's practically a vacation.
I'd stay for another loop, but someone is expecting me.
You got me here clean. Respect.
Thank you, child. Now let me get these groceries inside.
That final approach made sense. The whole ride feels resolved.
I'm free! Give that seat a minute before the next fare.
I did enjoy the ride. That doesn't change my tipping policy.
I'll remember that engine note. It had a great ending.
Right at the marked curb. I wish every driver did that.
You matched the map pin exactly. Satisfying.
Finally. I'm going to be pleasant for the next five minutes.
Three minutes early. I can work with that.
That's my building! I've never approached it from this side.
That was fun. The destination almost feels like an interruption.
We're on time. I've already prepared for the next delay.
Thanks. No, my name isn't a joke about the fare.
Hold still for one last frame. Now that's a proper ending.
A satisfactory delivery. You may consider that a compliment.
That porch has six objects I haven't met yet.
Thanks for the lift. I'll take the last few feet by wing.
This is it. Good driving.
You gave the brakes room to breathe. Nice finish.
What an ending! I want a replay of that last turn.
We finished. Tires still round. Solid result.
And there it is, folks: the stop everyone was waiting for.
Easy on the pedal at the end. My old crew would approve.
That quarry entrance is right there. I'm not saying why I'm excited.
You've reached my estate. Do not mistake the gate for the house.
I arrived despite your primitive navigation. Intriguing.
Excellent. The lab's alarm hasn't noticed me yet.
Good. The spring is just beyond those trees.
We made it. I can unclench my hands now, right?
Dag dag, plim! [This is the right lot, I think.]
Workshop! I stayed awake for almost all of it.
Your performance exceeded my prediction. Don't get used to hearing that.
Unload me here. The less you know about the door, the better.
A triumphant arrival! Please wait until I find my cape.
There are trees here. You should have led with that.
That's the buzzer, driver. You brought it home.
Easy stop. I learned late how much that matters.
Right on the spot. Nothing but net.
We made it! I only screamed twice. Maybe three times.
The route log looks clean. I'll send you my notes.
Precisely when we needed to be. That almost never happens.
The crate is humming softly. That's the good kind.
Good pull-in. You gave the trailer room even without one.
Well, that's the end of this set. Thanks for staying.
See that waterfall? A pump that never asks for a replacement seal.
The stars above this highway make my workshop ceiling look very small.
The cloud shadows move across the pasture at a remarkably soothing rate.
I lack a sensor for nostalgia, yet that old bridge produces something similar.
Those orchards belonged to my grandfather. He never put his name on them.
Leave the window open. The air here costs nothing, and that's rare.
The river has spent centuries cutting stone. At least someone shows ambition.
I dislike that sunrise. It makes even my ruined tower look hopeful.
The storm over the peaks has power. I can respect it.
That tiny village endures beneath the cliffs. Strength has many forms.
That thunderhead looks ready for battle. Wish I could challenge it.
We should picnic in that crater. Why are you looking at me like that?
The reeds by the pond hide three nests. Please use the quieter lane.
There is no fence around this meadow. The birds have chosen well.
Morning light on the lake. A perfect opening hand.
The canyon keeps one secret around each bend. I won't peek ahead.
See that hill? It needs a slide down the middle.
That rainbow landed right where I dropped my last crate. Coincidence?
The river is racing us through the gorge. It's winning.
I could run that trail at dawn and still stop to watch the deer.
How do they get the clouds to stay behind the hills?
That lake is blue from up here. Does it look blue to the fish?
The fog rolls off the water, and the entire valley makes its entrance.
We've got gold in the treetops and a full house of stars above.
Those red cliffs need a masked figure silhouetted on the rim.
No artist would get away with drawing clouds that strange. I love them.
The sea air almost makes me forget my entire morning.
That abandoned overlook has potential. For a quiet lunch, obviously.
See how the pines bend and still stand? There's your lesson.
The sun found a path through the clouds. You should be so observant.
The waterfall covers our footsteps. A lovely place to travel unseen.
Those birches mark the edge of an old hunting ground.
The river polished that granite for ages. My cousins would charge for it.
Those caves could shelter a whole clan. Mind the narrow entrance.
Interesting: the town grew around the old oak instead of removing it.
The mist makes every field seem endless. A lesson in perception.
The wheat looks like a sea of toast waiting to happen.
Beautiful orchard. I wonder whether they sell pies at the gate.
When I was young, my moon had forests like those.
The stars here are new to me. I find that comforting.
That farmhouse has a suspiciously large frying pan outside.
The sunrise over the grain field is almost too magnificent to peck at.
A border marked by flowers instead of walls. Imagine that.
The castle ruins belong to everyone now. They look better for it.
The herd moved through this clearing before dawn.
Snow on the upper trail. The lower path will stay open another week.
That harbor is quiet enough to hear the ropes tap against the masts.
One day I'm taking a whole afternoon off under those trees.
The moon has made a silver path across the lake. Don't disturb it.
That old grove keeps its own counsel. I admire discretion.
She wants to photograph the cliffs. I want to know what lies below.
For once we agree: the moonrise deserves a little silence.
Rain on the north ridge. Good news for the forest.
Look at the regrowth below that burned slope. It came back stronger.
The meadow is full of lupines. No one planted them; they just arrived.
I wish you could smell those pear blossoms from this side of the road.
That suspension bridge is elegant because it uses so little.
The solar roofs almost disappear into the hillside. That's good design.
There's room beside that stream to sit with someone without talking.
After a hard shift, the first stars over this ridge feel medicinal.
That orchard follows a precise grid. The wildflowers refuse to.
The horizon is almost level. Almost.
Those weeds broke through concrete. I think we would get along.
